newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle market calm after record Ks sales.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle market calm after record Ks sales.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was slow at $64.00 per cwt on Wednesday following active sales Tuesday and last Friday which pushed marketings in Kansas to a record weekly high, feedlot sources said.
Sales in Kansas set a record of 137,700 head, surpassing the previous record of 136,400 set the week ended Aug 22, 1996, USDA said. Sales on Wednesday were pegged at 1,600 head.

Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma sales totaled about 5,000 head, which brought the weekly volume near 134,000. Weekly sales in the Panhandle were well below the record of 196,000 set the week ended September 12, 1996.

Fed cattle prices this week slipped $1.00 from Friday and were down $2.00 from last week's top. Prices were pressured by large supplies of market-ready cattle and outlooks for continued expansion of cattle numbers well into the summer.
However, the fact that packers bought so many cattle this week had several feedlot managers optimistic that it suggested beef demand cauld be strong.
"It's encouraging the packer wants to take on this much inventory," a Panhandle feedlot manager said.
The active buying also helped keep feedlots close to being current in their marketings, they said.
